newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda says it repulses attack by Zairean troops.
newsitem.headline: Uganda says it repulses attack by Zairean troops.

text.p: Uganda said on Wednesday it killed three Zairean soldiers after they, backed by Zaire-based Ugandan dissidents, attacked two southwestern border posts.

In a statement in the name of the Ugandan cabinet, minister of state for international cooperation Martin Aliker said Uganda had repulsed the "enemy" and the Zairean soldiers and Ugandan dissidents retreated into Zaire from where they shelled Ugandan positions all day.

"The government of Uganda wishes it to be known that there were two armed attacks on its territory this morning. An army platoon was attacked at Karambi, which is seven km (four miles) northwest of Bwera. Another attack was at Mpondwe border post.
"These are two border tading centres between Uganda and Zaire in the southwest of Uganda. At Mpondwe, the enemy was repulsed, we killed three attackers," the statement said.
It added that Uganda had reinforced its positions and its army would defend its territorial integrity at all times.

Aliker would not say how many people had fled the border towns that came under shelling. He rejected suggestions that Uganda was targeted by Zaire because of its support for Banyamulenge ethnic Tutsi rebels who have seized several towns in eastern Zaire.
